source: FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, Swine Health Management, Volume 2: Guide to Prevent and Control Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome (RAP Publication 2012/27, Bangkok, 2012)
text: Before bringing new healthy pigs into a pen that previously held sick animals, all manure, urine, leftover feed, bedding, and body fluids must be completely removed and the surfaces power-washed, paying close attention to gratings, feeders, drinkers, and cracks or crevices where organic matter can hide. Once clean, disinfect the pen — the PRRS virus is easily killed by common disinfectants such as phenol and formaldehyde-based products. After disinfecting, let the facility fully dry, since this step is important for finishing off the virus and bacteria. Wait a minimum of 14 days after cleaning and disinfection before restocking the pen with new animals to avoid re-infection.
